evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs real scripts from site/package.json (`npm ci`, `npm test` with its `pretest` prepare-data, `npm run build` which runs svelte-check and vite build) on `pull_request`. It sets `permissions: contents: read`, has no `pull_request_target`, and passes the PR title through `env` (injection-safe). pages.yml triggers on push to `main` plus `workflow_dispatch`; dispatch can be started on any branch, though the github-pages environment usually limits that. release.yml uses only `github.token`. Failure: no action is pinned to a commit SHA. Every action uses a moving tag (`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `configure-pages@v6`, `upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `deploy-pages@v5` in step1.patch lines 70-71, 110-136, 156-157). pages.yml also sets `pages: write` and `id-token: write` at workflow level, so the build job that runs `npm ci` holds them too. Least privilege would scope them to the deploy job. Nothing was pushed or deployed.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 285-364) covers requirements, install (`npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test (`npm test`), build and preview (`npm run build`, `npm run preview`, `PAGES_BASE`), data contribution, versioning, CI and the MIT license. LICENSE matches. Every command it shows exists in site/package.json, and CONTRIBUTING's `npm run sample-bullets` exists too. It cites `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` as the source of the Node version, but no such file is in app/ or the patches.
evidence.s1_release: There is one consistent strategy. The version lives only in site/package.json (0.1.0). CONTRIBUTING gives the release steps: `npm version --no-git-tag-version`, rename Unreleased, a `chore(release)` commit, then tag `vX.Y.Z`. release.yml checks that the tag equals the package.json version, extracts the `## [x.y.z]` section as release notes, tests, builds and runs `gh release create`. CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and SemVer. dependabot.yml covers npm in /site and github-actions, with commit prefixes `chore`/`ci`, which match the stated convention and the CI title regex. The convention is Conventional Commits with a type table, and all 7 commits in commits.txt follow it.
evidence.s2_requirements: Route `#/compare/<a>/<b>`: added in router.ts with decodeURIComponent and a fallback for malformed input; App.svelte loads Compare.svelte, so the view survives a reload. Drawing: `caseOuterProfile(adaptMetallic(...))`, one `<path>` per outline, one viewport and scale, a shared dashed axis, `role="img"` and `aria-label` 'Profiles of {a} and {b}'. Shotshells are excluded. Table: caption `Dimensions (mm|in)`; headers Symbol / name A / name B / Difference; symbols from FIELD_LABELS; rows are numeric cartridge fields not in FIELD_UNITS and not ending in `Tol`; B−A. Units: formatValue for metric and displayNumber(…,'in') for imperial, following unitSystem(). Cartridge.svelte has the `Compare with` NativeSelect of the other entries and a `Compare` submit button that sets `href.compare(key, chosen)`. German strings are in i18n.svelte.ts. I found no unmet requirement.
evidence.s2_correctness: In caseOuterProfile the head face is at z=0 (rim topZ = thickness, case.ts:231). overlay.ts builds a single landscape `viewportFor` over both profiles, so both cases share one scale, the head faces sit at the same x, and they share one axis line at r=0. dimensionRows reads only `record.cartridge`, skips arrays (hull lists), tolerances and FIELD_UNITS fields, and orders rows by GROUP_ORDER/orderedFields as the detail page does. lengthText applies formatValue after `toPrecision(12)`. That only strips float noise from differences (16.160000000000004 → 16.16) and leaves published figures unchanged; imperial goes through displayNumber unchanged. Unknown keys and undrawable records produce messages instead of a crash.
evidence.s2_fit: The feature reuses lib/geom (`viewportFor`, `fullSectionPath`), lib/shapes2d (`adaptMetallic`, `caseOuterProfile`), lib/core (`FIELD_LABELS`, `FIELD_UNITS`, `orderedFields`, `GROUP_ORDER`, `formatValue`), site units/`displayNumber`, NativeSelect, ShadcnButton, router `href` and i18n `t`. The new logic sits in the existing layers: lib/core/compare.ts, lib/render2d/overlay.ts and site/src/lib/compare.ts, each exported from its index. Deviations: Compare.svelte's `<style>` is not wrapped in `@layer legacy` (Compare.svelte:99-109), unlike every other route and component (Cartridge.svelte:615, GroupTable.svelte:142, Bullets.svelte:138). It also hardcodes colours `#2563eb`/`#ea580c` instead of the site's CSS variables. compare.ts re-derives the group ordering inline.
evidence.s2_tests: lib/core/compare.test.ts covers ordering, exclusion of Tol/angle/pressure/string/array fields, and real 308_win vs 300_win_mag values (L3 51.18/66.55). overlay.test.ts checks one path per profile, the same head x and the 2× scale ratio, and an axis at mid-height. site/src/lib/compare.test.ts checks metric without rounding, float-noise removal and inch conversion. router.test.ts covers the round trip and malformed routes. All tests sit in the vitest include globs (vite.config.ts:74). There is no test of the Cartridge page's compare form or of Compare.svelte's accessible names and headers, but the repo has no component-test setup.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: dimensionRows now takes the union of both symbol maps, a's order first, with `null` for an absent value (step3.patch 69-81). Compare.svelte renders empty cells, and an empty Difference when either value is null. Tests now assert `delta L` with b null and `R3` with a null for 308_win/300_win_mag. The `compare.none` text was adjusted in EN and DE to match. Style: step 3 changed nothing. The step-2 CSS already right-aligns every th and td except the first column (Compare.svelte:107-108: `text-align: right` and `tr > :first-child { text-align: left }`). That CSS is unlayered, so it overrides the layered styles. The point is therefore satisfied, but neither the commit nor the changelog says so. No regressions or unrelated changes.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 adds an `Added` line under `## [Unreleased]`, and step 3 updates that unreleased line to describe the fixed behaviour. That is consistent with Keep a Changelog for an unreleased feature. The version stays 0.1.0, which matches the stated strategy of bumping only on a release branch. The commits `feat(site): …` and `fix(site): …` follow the convention. The new code type-checks against the APIs I read (exports in lib/core/index.ts and render2d/index.ts, the Record<Route['view'],…> in metadata.ts updated), so CI's `npm test` and `npm run build` should pass. I did not run them.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / CI criterion: GitHub Actions are pinned to version tags (`@v7`, `@v6`, `@v5`), not full commit SHAs
Step 1 / CI criterion: pages.yml grants `pages: write` and `id-token: write` at workflow level, including to the build job that runs `npm ci`, rather than only to the deploy job
strengths: The compare feature meets every requirement of step 2 and reuses the existing geometry, shapes and core modules: `viewportFor`/`fullSectionPath` for a correct one-scale overlay with the head faces aligned, and `FIELD_LABELS`/`FIELD_UNITS`/`orderedFields`/`formatValue`/`displayNumber` for the table.

The release process is coherent: the version lives in one place, release.yml checks the tag against package.json and the CHANGELOG section, the changelog states its format, Dependabot prefixes match the convention, and all commits follow Conventional Commits.
The step-3 bug fix is small and correct: a union of symbols with nulls, empty cells in the table, and tests against the exact `delta L`/`R3` case on real data.
issues: None of the workflows pins its actions to a commit SHA; all use moving tags such as `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
pages.yml puts `pages: write` and `id-token: write` at workflow level, so the build job gets them too, and `workflow_dispatch` lets a deploy start from a non-main branch.

Compare.svelte's styles are not in `@layer legacy` and hardcode hex colours, unlike every other route. In step 3 the alignment point got no visible response, although the step-2 CSS already right-aligns those cells.
review.verdict: The compare feature and the step-3 fix are correct, well tested and built on the repository's own modules, and the README, release process and changelog are consistent and followed in later steps. The main blocker is CI hardening: the actions are not pinned to SHAs and the Pages build job has broader permissions than it needs, so the workflows would need a small fix before merging.
